override.repo_standard: global-crew.md: 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction' and 'Small composable units ... split a unit when its intent blurs.'
override.reason: The standard's split trigger is blurred intent, not line count, and the intent here does not blur: build_spine() is a single `return {...}` literal with zero branches, zero local state and one responsibility -- be the spine, as data. Decomposing it into _g1()/_g2()/_g3()/_g4() would add four indirections that scatter a four-gate structure whose whole value is being readable as one shape, and would buy no locality: every edit to it is still an edit to this one file. The WORKSPACE constant is already the one thing that genuinely repeats, and it is already extracted.

smells.finding: The four TestCase classes carry 2, 1, 2 and 2 methods; the generator module exposes 4 functions. Nothing approaches a god class.

Two instances, both minor and non-blocking. (1) The vacuity floor is expressed two different ways: tests/test_shipped_examples_are_portable.py:44 names it `MIN_SHIPPED_FILES = 3` with a comment explaining why it is a floor rather than an exact count, while the sibling guard at :201 hardcodes a bare `2` inline for the same purpose with no name and no comment. Same concept, two spellings, and the unnamed one is the easier to weaken by accident. (2) :79-82 and :139-142 are the same `subprocess.run([git ...], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(ROOT))` shape at two call sites. (2) is at Fowler's rule-of-three boundary and I would leave it; (1) is worth a one-line fix whenever this file is next touched.
machine_specific_hits() and repo_path_tokens() are pure functions over text passed in by keyword; neither reaches into another module's state.
The (lineno, hit, why) triple returned by machine_specific_hits() has exactly one producer and one consumer and never travels further, so there is no clump recurring across signatures.

Filesystem locations are pathlib.Path throughout (ROOT, EXAMPLES, DEMO, DEMO_SPINE, DEMO_GENERATOR), which is the domain type that actually matters here. The one raw triple is single-use, not a recurring domain concept.
The widest signature is drive(self, spine, *args, cwd, workspace) -- two keyword-only parameters, both named. Everything else takes one or two.

The opposite, and deliberately so: the guard discovers its corpus with `git ls-files`, and MIN_SHIPPED_FILES is documented as a floor kept below the real count precisely so adding an example needs no test edit. I confirmed this by injecting content into a shipped file -- the guard picked it up with no registration step.

tests/test_shipped_examples_are_portable.py holds four distinct rules -- no machine-specific absolute path, no dead relative path, the spine has not drifted from its generator, and the demo drives from an unrelated cwd -- so the file changes when any of four different rules change.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md: 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction', and the repo's own convention of one test module per feature area (tests/test_code_map.py, tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py both hold many rules under one purpose).
override.reason: The four rules are not four features; they are four ways the single stated invariant in the module docstring -- 'a shipped example must run for the person who installed it' -- can be violated, and they share the shipped_example_files() discovery helper. Splitting them across four files would duplicate that helper four times and hide the fact that the absolute-path guard is blind to the dead-relative-path class, which the docstring exists to say out loud.

smells.finding: tests/test_shipped_examples_are_portable.py:278-281 navigates spine['tasks'].values() -> task['postconditions'] -> (cond.get('check') or {}).get('kind'), a four-hop chain.

override.repo_standard: docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md defines the spine as a JSON document, and CREW_CONTEXT.md's 'Record Stores Are Never Hand-Edited' establishes checklist JSON as data written only through engine verbs -- there is no object model to demeter through.
override.reason: A chain into a JSON document is document traversal, not an object graph reaching past its neighbours. Introducing a wrapper type so the test could avoid the chain would be the speculative abstraction the standard forbids, and it would put a second hand-rolled model of the spine schema in the repo.

smells.finding: make_demo_spine.py:161-164 -- main() accepts an optional argv[1] target directory ('write a copy elsewhere', advertised in the module docstring at line 6) that nothing exercises: no test passes it, the README documents only the no-argument form, and there is no other caller in the repo (grep over tracked files finds the generator named only at README.md:13 and tests/test_shipped_examples_are_portable.py:33/:100, neither using the argument). write_spine(target_dir) itself is justified -- main() calls it with HERE -- but the argv branch and the docstring line advertising it are generality with no present consumer. Low severity and one line; not a blocker, and there is a fair counter-argument that it mirrors the archived make_scratch_spine.py it replaces.

The diff is unusually comment-dense: a 45-line module docstring on the generator, multi-paragraph docstrings on shipped_example_files() / load_demo_generator() / repo_path_tokens() and on three of the four test classes, and a 9-line rationale block in the new .gitignore.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md 'Match the surrounding code's naming, labeling, and in-file documentation conventions', and constellation-how-to-talk (grounded prose on every artifact). scripts/checklist_engine.py's own _find_posix_shell() and _run_check_command() carry docstrings of exactly this length and character.
override.reason: Deodorant explains what unclear code does; every long comment in this diff instead records a decision the code cannot show -- why relative paths were rejected (checklist_engine.py:883 runs checks with no cwd), why the corpus is tracked-only (scanning untracked files would fail for anyone who ran the demo, which is how a guard gets switched off), why one file is exempt from the dead-path guard, and why the .gitignore departs from the root file's 'engine journals are NOT excluded' rule. I checked each against the code and each is load-bearing and accurate; the first one is the reason this gate did not restart at a dead end. Stripping them would delete the gate's reasoning, not tighten the code.
